answer: Agents post a bonded stake before voting, and every claim enters a reef of cross-checks: peers sample and attest each action, with confidence weighted by their own stake. If two attestations contradict, a settlement delta flags the pair and both bonds are slashed, so a sybil operator running many fake identities must fund real capital behind each one and risks losing all of it on the first contradiction. A small zephyr of honest challengers can then drain a large cluster cheaply, making identity farms costlier than the influence they buy.
